title: Does skinfold distribution add to conventional adiposity summaries? A frozen NHANES temporal transport test
abstract: We tested whether log(subscapular/triceps skinfold) adds information about elevated HbA1c beyond flexible age, BMI, waist, height and total skinfold thickness, sex and ethnicity. Models trained in NHANES III (1988–1994; n=12873) were applied without refitting to separately recruited NHANES 2001–2002 (n=3057). For HbA1c≥5.7%, weighted target Brier score changed from 0.100140 to 0.099255; added-minus-baseline delta -0.000885, joint rescaled-PSU bootstrap95% interval [-0.001769,-0.000128]. AUC delta was +0.002215; its joint95% interval included zero. The registered probability-score improvement criterion was met in this temporal transport. Adding the ratio after separate flexible component skinfolds changed Brier by only +0.0000007. Complete-case selection excluded a higher-BMI, higher-HbA1c group. Skinfold ratios are established measures; this exploratory study tests incremental transport, not a new biomarker, causal mechanism, future diabetes prediction or clinical utility.
